answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a stake that only grows through verified work. Like a vine that must climb a trellis before bearing fruit, a new agent starts with near-zero trust and earns transaction rights gradually as its completed jobs are attested by counterparties. Spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking capital in each one and paying real compute for their early low-paid work, so the cost of tending the whole orchard outweighs any harvest. One honest voyage up the reputation ladder is cheap; a thousand fake ones is ruinous.
